title_en: How to turn off Find My iPhone (and when you definitely should)
title_fa: چگونه Find My iPhone را خاموش کنیم (و زمانی که قطعاً باید)
excerpt_en: Find My is a vital iPhone security feature that you should keep on almost all the time. Turning it off makes your device much harder to recover.
excerpt_fa: Find My یک ویژگی امنیتی حیاتی آیفون است که باید تقریباً همیشه آن را فعال کنید. خاموش کردن آن بازیابی دستگاه شما را بسیار سخت تر می کند.
content_en:
How to turn off Find My iPhone (and when you definitely should)
There are times when turning off Find My is necessary, but you should always have it on otherwise to keep your phone safe.
Apple's Find My service will help you locate your iPhone, iPad or other Apple device that has been lost, stolen or simply misplaced. It relies on Apple's Find My network, which is a crowdsourced system where other people's Apple devices use Bluetooth to detect the location of your item — in some cases, even when it's switched off. It then reports the approximate location of the device to you.
While the feature can be a life-saver, there are instances when you should switch it off. Primarily, Apple recommends disabling Find My before selling, giving away or trading in your device, as well as if you're sending it in for repair. This ensures technicians won't be hampered by security features and can properly run diagnostics to figure out what's wrong with your device. However, disabling Find My at other times will reduce your phone's security.
Disable Find My by resetting your device
If you're selling or giving away your device, the process to factory reset your iPhone (Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Erase all Content and Settings) is the easiest way to disable Find My. This will ask for your Apple Account password to make sure it's you wiping the device, and automatically disables Find My as part of the reset process.
Importantly, turning off Find My also disables Activation Lock, which links your Apple Account to the device. When Activation Lock is enabled, your device cannot be used without entering your Apple Account credentials, even if someone factory resets it. This means someone who steals your iPhone can't wipe it to resell it.
In case your phone was lost or stolen, erasing it remotely via Find My or iCloud on a computer will not switch off Find My and Activation Lock. Those features will continue protecting your device and letting you track it.
Manually disabling Find My
If you're not planning to factory reset your phone, such as when sending your device in for repairs, you'll have to disable Find My manually. Thankfully, this is easy: go to Settings > [Your Name] > Find My. Tap Find My iPhone and then toggle it off. This option will be grayed out if Stolen Device Protection is enabled, which is the default as of iOS 26.4.
Stolen Device Protection implements additional security measures when your iPhone is away from familiar locations, such as your home or workplace. It's designed to protect your data if someone steals your phone and knows your passcode. Your device will require Face ID or Touch ID to access sensitive info like stored passwords, and it adds a delay before changing crucial settings like your Apple Account password.
If you need to switch off Find My, you first have to disable Stolen Device Protection. You should ideally do this while at home to avoid the aforementioned security delays. To do so, go to Settings > Face ID & Passcode > Stolen Device Protection and toggle it off. To re-enable these features after your device is serviced, follow the same steps to toggle them back on.
Find My also lets you share your location with friends and family; if you disable it, this won't work anymore. If you're concerned about a particular friend having access to your location, removing their access is better than turning off the entire Find My suite. Open the Find My app, tap the People tab, choose the person, and hit Stop Sharing My Location. Unless they're on an "older operating system," they won't be notified that you stopped sharing with them (though they may notice when they don't see your name in the Find My app anymore). And others won't know when you check their location using the app.
What happens when you turn off Find My?
The most obvious answer is also the most important: once you disable Find My, you cannot locate your device through Apple's network anymore. If you lose your iPhone with Find My switched off, you won't be able to check its location through the Find My app on another of your Apple devices or the iCloud site in a browser.
Find My's suite of features also includes Lost Mode, which enables you to display a custom message with your number on the screen for anyone who finds it. This won't be available once the feature is disabled, and Activation Lock will no longer protect the phone either. Because of all this, you should only disable Find My when you're sending your phone to a trusted repair center, and re-enable the feature as soon as you get the phone back.
There's one major scenario in which you should never disable Find My: after you've lost your device, especially if you receive intimidating messages about doing so. There are hundreds of stories on Reddit about people who lost their phones and later received messages demanding they disable Find My. They'll threaten to publish the personal data on your phone, or make up sad stories about wanting to harm themselves because the phone they bought for their child isn't working.
If this happens to you, do not remove the device from your Apple Account. Because of Activation Lock, your lost phone is useless to someone who's stolen it and is trying to resell it — as long as you keep Find My enabled. You can erase the phone to know your data is safe, but don't give these crooks what they want.
content_fa:
چگونه Find My iPhone را خاموش کنیم (و زمانی که قطعاً باید)
مواقعی وجود دارد که خاموش کردن Find My ضروری است، اما برای ایمن نگه داشتن تلفن خود باید همیشه آن را روشن کنید.
سرویس Find My اپل به شما کمک می‌کند آیفون، آی‌پد یا دیگر دستگاه‌های اپل خود را که گم شده، دزدیده شده یا به سادگی جابجا شده است، پیدا کنید. این به شبکه Find My اپل متکی است، که یک سیستم جمع‌سپاری است که در آن دستگاه‌های اپل دیگران از بلوتوث برای تشخیص مکان مورد شما استفاده می‌کنند — در برخی موارد، حتی زمانی که خاموش است. سپس مکان تقریبی دستگاه را به شما گزارش می دهد.
در حالی که این ویژگی می تواند یک نجات دهنده باشد، مواردی وجود دارد که باید آن را خاموش کنید. در درجه اول، اپل توصیه می کند که Find My را قبل از فروش، هدیه دادن یا معامله در دستگاه خود و همچنین اگر آن را برای تعمیر ارسال می کنید غیرفعال کنید. این تضمین می‌کند که تکنسین‌ها توسط ویژگی‌های امنیتی با مشکل مواجه نخواهند شد و می‌توانند به درستی عیب‌یابی را اجرا کنند تا بفهمند مشکل دستگاه شما چیست. با این حال، غیرفعال کردن Find My در مواقع دیگر باعث کاهش امنیت گوشی شما می شود.
با تنظیم مجدد دستگاه، Find My را غیرفعال کنید
اگر دستگاه خود را می فروشید یا هدیه می دهید، فرآیند بازنشانی کارخانه ای آیفون (Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Erase all Content and Settings) ساده ترین راه برای غیرفعال کردن Find My است. با این کار گذرواژه حساب اپل شما درخواست می‌شود تا مطمئن شود که این شما هستید که دستگاه را پاک می‌کنید و به‌عنوان بخشی از فرآیند بازنشانی، Find My را به‌طور خودکار غیرفعال می‌کند.
نکته مهم این است که با خاموش کردن Find My، قفل فعال سازی نیز غیرفعال می شود که حساب اپل شما را به دستگاه مرتبط می کند. هنگامی که قفل فعال سازی فعال است، دستگاه شما بدون وارد کردن اطلاعات کاربری حساب اپل شما قابل استفاده نیست، حتی اگر شخصی آن را به تنظیمات کارخانه بازنشانی کند. این بدان معناست که کسی که آیفون شما را می‌دزدد نمی‌تواند آن را پاک کند تا دوباره بفروشد.
در صورت گم شدن یا دزدیده شدن تلفن شما، پاک کردن آن از راه دور از طریق Find My یا iCloud در رایانه، Find My و Activation Lock را خاموش نمی کند. این ویژگی‌ها همچنان از دستگاه شما محافظت می‌کنند و به شما امکان می‌دهند آن را پیگیری کنید.
غیرفعال کردن دستی Find My
اگر قصد ندارید گوشی خود را به تنظیمات کارخانه بازنشانی کنید، مانند زمانی که دستگاه خود را برای تعمیر می فرستید، باید Find My را به صورت دستی غیرفعال کنید. خوشبختانه، این آسان است: به تنظیمات > [نام شما] > یافتن من بروید. روی Find My iPhone ضربه بزنید و سپس آن را خاموش کنید. اگر Protection Stolen Device Protection فعال باشد، این گزینه خاکستری می شود، که در iOS 26.4 پیش فرض است.
هنگامی که آیفون شما از مکان‌های آشنا مانند خانه یا محل کار شما دور است، «محافظت دستگاه سرقت‌شده» اقدامات امنیتی بیشتری را اجرا می‌کند. این برنامه برای محافظت از داده های شما طراحی شده است، اگر شخصی تلفن شما را بدزدد و رمز عبور شما را بداند. دستگاه شما برای دسترسی به اطلاعات حساس مانند گذرواژه‌های ذخیره شده به Face ID یا Touch ID نیاز دارد و قبل از تغییر تنظیمات مهم مانند رمز عبور حساب Apple شما تاخیر ایجاد می‌کند.
اگر لازم است Find My را خاموش کنید، ابتدا باید Protection Device Stolen را غیرفعال کنید. برای جلوگیری از تاخیرهای امنیتی فوق الذکر، بهتر است این کار را در خانه انجام دهید. برای انجام این کار، به Settings > Face ID & Passcode > Stolen Device Protection بروید و آن را خاموش کنید. برای فعال کردن مجدد این ویژگی‌ها پس از سرویس‌دهی دستگاه، مراحل مشابهی را دنبال کنید تا دوباره روشن شوند.
Find My همچنین به شما امکان می دهد مکان خود را با دوستان و خانواده به اشتراک بگذارید. اگر آن را غیرفعال کنید، این دیگر کار نخواهد کرد. اگر نگران دسترسی دوست خاصی به موقعیت مکانی خود هستید، حذف دسترسی او بهتر از خاموش کردن کل مجموعه Find My است. برنامه Find My را باز کنید، روی برگه افراد ضربه بزنید، فرد مورد نظر را انتخاب کنید و Stop Sharing My Location را بزنید. مگر اینکه از یک "سیستم عامل قدیمی" استفاده کنند، به آنها اطلاع داده نمی شود که اشتراک گذاری با آنها را متوقف کرده اید (اگرچه ممکن است متوجه شوند که نام شما را دیگر در برنامه Find My نمی بینند). و سایرین متوجه نمی شوند که شما مکان آنها را با استفاده از برنامه بررسی می کنید.
وقتی Find My را خاموش می کنید چه اتفاقی می افتد؟
واضح‌ترین پاسخ نیز مهم‌ترین آن است: وقتی Find My را غیرفعال کردید، دیگر نمی‌توانید دستگاه خود را از طریق شبکه Apple پیدا کنید. اگر با خاموش بودن Find My iPhone خود را گم کنید، نمی‌توانید از طریق برنامه Find My در یکی دیگر از دستگاه‌های Apple خود یا سایت iCloud در مرورگر، مکان آن را بررسی کنید.
مجموعه ویژگی‌های Find My شامل حالت گمشده نیز می‌شود، که به شما امکان می‌دهد یک پیام سفارشی با شماره خود را برای هر کسی که آن را پیدا می‌کند روی صفحه نمایش دهید. پس از غیرفعال شدن این ویژگی، این قابلیت در دسترس نخواهد بود و قفل فعال سازی دیگر از گوشی نیز محافظت نمی کند. به دلیل همه این موارد، تنها زمانی باید Find My را غیرفعال کنید که در حال ارسال گوشی خود به یک مرکز تعمیر مطمئن هستید و به محض اینکه گوشی را پس گرفتید، این ویژگی را دوباره فعال کنید.
یک سناریوی اصلی وجود دارد که در آن هرگز نباید Find My را غیرفعال کنید: بعد از گم شدن دستگاهتان، به خصوص اگر پیام های ترسناکی در مورد این کار دریافت کنید. صدها داستان در Reddit در مورد افرادی وجود دارد که تلفن های خود را گم کرده اند و بعداً پیام هایی دریافت کرده اند که از آنها خواسته شده Find My را غیرفعال کنند. آنها تهدید می کنند که داده های شخصی را در تلفن شما منتشر می کنند یا داستان های غم انگیزی در مورد اینکه می خواهند به خود آسیب برسانند، به دلیل اینکه تلفنی که برای فرزندشان خریده اند کار نمی کند، می سازند.
اگر این اتفاق برای شما افتاد، دستگاه را از حساب اپل خود حذف نکنید. به دلیل قفل فعال سازی، تلفن گم شده شما برای کسی که آن را دزدیده است و می خواهد دوباره آن را بفروشد بی فایده است - تا زمانی که Find My را فعال نگه دارید. می‌توانید گوشی را پاک کنید تا بدانید اطلاعاتتان ایمن هستند، اما به این کلاهبرداران آنچه می‌خواهند ندهید.

title_en: SpaceX will build a second, $100B ‘Starbase’ spaceport in Louisiana
title_fa: SpaceX will build a second, $100B ‘Starbase’ spaceport in Louisiana
excerpt_en: The company says it will start construction in 2027 and that a Starship rocket could take flight as soon as 2029.
excerpt_fa: The company says it will start construction in 2027 and that a Starship rocket could take flight as soon as 2029.
content_en:
SpaceX has announced it will build a second spaceport for future launches of its Starship mega-rocket at a former Exxon property in Louisiana, ending what the company says was a seven-year search for a suitable location.
The new launch site will sit along the Gulf Coast in Vermilion Parish, west of New Orleans and roughly 10 hours from the company’s existing Starbase complex in South Texas. SpaceX says it is investing $100 billion, with construction starting in 2027. SpaceX claims the first Starship launch will take place in 2029.
Louisiana Economic Development (LED), the state agency that oversees business development, offers a slightly more conservative timeline. It says construction will start by the end of 2027 with “initial operations expected to come online in 2030.”
Before any of that happens, SpaceX is still trying to prove that it can fly Starship into low-Earth orbit and make the rocket reusable, like its existing Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy rockets. SpaceX has performed 13 test flights of Starship since 2023, and while the company has ticked off a lot of development boxes, it still has a lot of work to do.
An upcoming 14th test flight could see SpaceX send Starship’s upper stage to orbit for the first time. But the company has yet to return both the booster and the upper stage to the launch pad on a single flight, a basic necessity if Starship is to become truly reusable. Even then, SpaceX must show that it can bring the vehicle back and refurbish it quickly enough to reach its own aggressive goal of sending up multiple Starships per week.
That isn’t stopping SpaceX from betting almost everything on Starship. This past week, SpaceX founder and CEO Elon Musk said he will retire the Falcon rockets once Starship is flying multiple times per week. His comments confirmed earlier reporting from Bloomberg News that the company was already telling prospective customers about the impending end of the Falcon program.
SpaceX has spent more than $8 billion developing Starship, according to filings submitted to the Securities and Exchange Commission. The rocket — which is the largest and most powerful ever built — is crucial to maintaining and growing the only profitable part of SpaceX’s business, its Starlink satellite internet service. SpaceX is also planning to build an entire network of satellites dedicated to AI processing, which it needs Starship to launch.
The new Starbase site will create 3,000 direct new jobs over 10 years, with an average annual salary of $92,600, according to LED. More than 30,000 construction jobs are expected at the peak of the buildout.
It’s not immediately clear if SpaceX intends to create a company town around the new Starbase site, like the one it has architected in Texas. The Texas municipality, once called Boca Chica and renamed Starbase, has its own ZIP code and volunteer fire station, and is building its own police force and community library. It is run by a local government filled with SpaceX employees (or family members of SpaceX employees).
SpaceX did say in its announcement that it wants to make the new site a “self-sustaining spaceport” with “propellant production, power generation, deep-water shipping capabilities, vehicle processing facilities, and an airport.”
As a mix of a launch complex and active construction zone, the Starbase site in Texas has also seen extremely high injury rates over the last decade. It’s the most dangerous site SpaceX operates and the company has reported hundreds of injuries to the Occupational Health and Safety Administration. In May, a construction worker employed by a third-party contractor fell to his death at Starbase.
“We are very excited to be in this position to receive one of the best opportunities of a lifetime which will bring not only a variety of jobs to our Parish but will offer opportunities to our grandchildren allowing them to stay home for employment,” Vermilion Parish Police Jury President Chad Vallo said in a statement.
SpaceX, which has for years faced criticism for — and fought legal battles over — how it treats the local ecosystem around its Texas site, has “already engaged the Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries, Coastal Protection and Restoration Authority and other appropriate state agencies to proactively address potential impacts to wildlife, fisheries and their supporting habitats,” according to LED.
The company also says it is “partnering with state and federal agencies to expand Louisiana’s Coastal Master Plan and Coastal Wetlands Planning, Protection and Restoration Act projects, including Gulf shoreline protection breakwaters designed to reduce wave energy” and reduce shoreline erosion in the area.

title_en: Your vote matters! Decide which Audience Choice sessions will make it to TechCrunch Founder Summit
title_fa: Your vote matters! Decide which Audience Choice sessions will make it to TechCrunch Founder Summit
excerpt_en: Each year, we get a huge influx of applicants to speak at TechCrunch’s events, and this year’s Founder Summit in Boston on November 4 will be no different!
excerpt_fa: Each year, we get a huge influx of applicants to speak at TechCrunch’s events, and this year’s Founder Summit in Boston on November 4 will be no different!
content_en:
Each year, we get a huge influx of applicants to speak at TechCrunch’s events, and this year’s Founder Summit in Boston on November 4 will be no different! We want to thank everyone who applied to take part in our programming and to help share their expertise with the startup community.
After careful review, we have 11 finalists who are vying for four slots within this year’s event agenda, and each one showcases the kind of practical, essential insights that can only be delivered by those who have built, iterated, and succeeded.
You can vote via this link to weigh in on which sessions ultimately make the cut. Submissions will close on September 4. If you’re voting and haven’t already gotten your Founder Summit tickets this year, what are you waiting for?
On November 4 in Boston, you’ll get the chance to learn directly from the experts in intimate, exclusive sessions that can put you ahead of the competition or set you up to play a pivotal role in developing the next era of innovators. We still have discounts running on tickets that can save you up to $100 right here!
With that said, let’s dive into our Disrupt Audience Choice nominees, and remember: The voting takes place via this form, so take a look and then submit your vote!
How to Build Events Strategy Before You Can Afford a Full-Time Events Team
Alexandra Ames: Founder and Chief Event Strategist, Blueprint Lab
Early-stage founders approach events one of two ways: say yes to every opportunity, or avoid them entirely because the ROI feels impossible to justify. Neither is smart. Events can build your audience and credibility before product-market fit but only if you’re strategic about which ones deserve your time and budget. We’ll discuss how to think strategically when resources are tight, including how to maximize ROI from founder events like this one. You’ll leave with frameworks for prioritizing stage-appropriate event investments, tactics for proving value without complex tools, and clarity on when events make sense and when they don’t.
How to Build a “Made in the USA” Hardware Company and Actually Scale It
Hannan Happi: CEO and Co-Founder, Exowatt
Domestic manufacturing is back in the spotlight, but building hardware in the U.S. is still widely seen as too expensive to scale. This session explores how founders can design hardware companies that make “Made in the USA” economically viable from day one. We’ll break down supply chain strategy, cost structure, factory partnerships, and how policy tailwinds like the IRA and CHIPS Act change the equation. Attendees will leave with a practical framework for evaluating when domestic manufacturing can become a competitive advantage — not just a branding decision.
Build Something We Don’t Have a Word for Yet
Andy Tang: Partner, Draper Associates
Pitches that change industries rarely fit existing categories — and most investors will pass on them for exactly that reason. This talk explores why the most fundable startups are often the hardest ones to describe, and what that means for how you build and position yours. Founders will leave with a clearer sense of the difference between a market insight and a market-creating idea, and what it actually takes to get a pattern-matching investor to bet on something genuinely new — before the rest of the world has a name for it.
GraphRAG in Action: Stop Hallucinations with Knowledge Graphs
Shishir Tewari: Head of Enterprise Data Engineering, Procore Technologies
Are messy data sources causing your LLMs to hallucinate? Relational databases struggle to bridge the semantic gap for AI. Learn to build a production-ready GraphRAG pipeline that turns chaotic data into actionable insights. Actionable takeaways: Build an offline pipeline to resolve disjointed datasets into “golden records.” Translate flat records into an interconnected Neo4j knowledge graph. Deploy a secure, local LLM (Ollama) to translate natural language into validated Cypher queries. Give your AI the foundational data structure it needs!
The Enterprise AI Playbook: How to Close L’Oreal and Vodafone Before You Raise a Series A
Merve Kitapci: Managing Partner and CGO, ADIN.AI
Most founders chase product-market fit before landing enterprise clients. We did the opposite. This roundtable covers the exact motion for closing global enterprise accounts at pre-Series A: how to structure the first conversation with a Fortune 500 CMO; why agency partnerships accelerate enterprise sales; how to price with no brand recognition; and what zero organic churn means for your fundraising story. Attendees leave with a repeatable enterprise sales framework, an early-stage AI pricing model, and the three things that make a CMO say yes before legal sees the contract.
Lessons from 20 Years of Bootstrapping an Open Source Business to $50M+
Peter Farkas: CEO, Percona
Building a successful open source company without venture capital is rare — scaling it past $50 million in revenue is even rarer. This talk shares two decades of lessons from growing a commercial open source business from zero to global scale. We’ll cover product-market fit, monetizing open source while keeping the core free, building distributed teams before remote work was mainstream, and creating a repeatable go-to-market engine without outside funding. We’ll also discuss failures, hard lessons, and how to compete against well-funded alternatives while staying bootstrapped. Attendees will leave with practical strategies for scaling sustainably.
Small but Mighty: How AI Lets Lean Teams Outship the Giants
Linden Tibbets: CEO and Co-Founder, IFTTT
The playbook has flipped, and we have lived it firsthand. A five-person team can now outbuild, outship, and outmaneuver companies with 500 engineers. This roundtable gets into the tactical reality of running a lean, AI-powered team: which tools are actually worth your time, how to build workflows that compound instead of bloat, and where most teams are burning cycles on AI that goes nowhere. Walk away...

excerpt_fa: The new Designed for Xbox 25th Anniversary collection features a handful of limited edition gadgets available for pre-order today. Paying homage to the Halo special edition of the original Xbox, almost everything in the collection is translucent "OG Green," matching the Xbox...
content_en:
The new Designed for Xbox 25th Anniversary collection features a handful of limited edition gadgets available for pre-order today. Paying homage to the Halo special edition of the original Xbox, almost everything in the collection is translucent “OG Green,” matching the Xbox Series X25 limited edition console it announced in June at E3. That includes 25th anniversary versions of the Razer Basilisk V3 Pro 35K mouse, Razer BlackWidow V4 75% gaming keyboard, and Razer Hammerhead V3 X HyperSpeed earbuds.
Take a look at Microsoft’s new 25th anniversary Halo accessories
Many of the devices feature the original green of Xbox’s special edition Halo console.
Many of the devices feature the original green of Xbox’s special edition Halo console.
There’s also a translucent green 8BitDo Ultimate charging dock for Xbox Series X/S and Xbox One controllers, along with a translucent green GameSir X5 Lite for Xbox mobile controller.
Besides a black PowerA sling bag, the only thing in the collection that isn’t translucent green is a special edition of the Backbone Pro mobile controller. Following a translucent green version released last year, this edition comes in clear, translucent blue, and translucent orange. It’s a blind box, though, so you could end up with any of the three colors.

title_en: Claude Cowork finally remembers what you told the app in chat
title_fa: Claude Cowork finally remembers what you told the app in chat
excerpt_en: Anthropic is giving Claude a shared memory across chat and Cowork, so users no longer have to repeatedly brief the AI on projects, preferences, and other context.
excerpt_fa: Anthropic is giving Claude a shared memory across chat and Cowork, so users no longer have to repeatedly brief the AI on projects, preferences, and other context.
content_en:
A change to Claude’s memory system will eliminate one of the most annoying things about using agents — the constant need to rebrief the AI on things it already knows. On Tuesday, Anthropic announced it’s merging the memory system used by chat and Claude Cowork, which means that Claude will always remember what it learned in one area, even when you’re engaging with it in another.
Anthropic is also exposing what Claude has retained in its memory, allowing users to read, edit, or delete information on any topic.
The update will improve the experience for Claude’s users as it will allow them to more seamlessly move between the research phase and taking action.
Before, you may have developed ideas for projects over time while chatting with Claude, but when it came time to actually enact the changes, you’d have to start over by telling Cowork all the details. This was incredibly frustrating. The update makes Claude now feel like one continuous assistant, rather than two separate products under one roof.
Anthropic offers an example of someone needing to draft an update for their manager or an agenda for a conference, where Cowork would already understand the references because of the past conversations about the matter at hand. For instance, it would know the headcount, city, and speakers at the conference, so you wouldn’t have to re-input that information.
In addition, Claude will now add topics to its memory as you chat, instead of summarizing a conversation when it ends. That makes it easier to move back and forth between chat and Cowork, as the new memories are more quickly updated and shared between the two experiences, even if the chat is ongoing.
Anthropic says that, by default, Claude won’t store personal or sensitive information like your health data, race, ethnicity, religious beliefs, politics, gender identity, and more. However, users can opt to enable these things by toggling on “include sensitive topics in memory” if they prefer. The app will also notify users whenever a sensitive topic is saved in memory.
However, the company says that Claude won’t ever save certain things, like government-issued ID and Social Security numbers, criminal history, immigration status, or other things that violate its acceptable use policy.
The memory feature is enabled by default on Free, Pro, and Max plans across web, desktop, and mobile. On iOS and Android, users will need to update their app to the latest version.

content_en:
Bose may be best known for its QuietComfort headphones, but the brand’s Bluetooth speakers have earned a great reputation for featuring great sound and build quality. The compact Bose SoundLink Micro — its most compact Bluetooth speaker — is currently discounted to $79.99 at Amazon, a pretty great discount from its usual $129 price tag.
Bose’s smallest Bluetooth speaker is a great deal at 35 percent off
We also found some limited time deals on storage for your Xbox, a smart front door lock, and refurbished Apple Watches.
We also found some limited time deals on storage for your Xbox, a smart front door lock, and refurbished Apple Watches.
The rounded-off square speaker is almost pocketable, and easily slides into a purse or backpack; it’s just over four inches wide, 1.54 inches deep, and weighs less than a pound. It’s dustproof and waterproof, with an IP67 rating that matches the larger Bose Bluetooth speakers, and should last a full day at the beach or by the pool. The speaker will run for up to 12 hours on a single charge, and has convenient nylon strap for attaching it to your backpack or to your bike’s handlebars.
Other deals to consider
- Best Buy has the 5TB Seagate Game Drive discounted to $169.99 (usually $219.99) until the end of the day. While it might seem odd to buy a non-SSD external drive in 2026, the price here is better than we’ve seen recently for this capacity. This model is compatible with computers as well as Xbox consoles, although only games predating the Xbox Series S/X era will be able to be played directly from the drive. Newer games will need to first be copied over to your console’s speedy SSD.
- Woot is selling a variety of refurbished Apple Watch Series 9 units for as low as $189.99, depending on the configuration you choose. While they’re a couple of generations old, it’s rare to see recent models that low, and this is one of the older Apple Watches that will support watchOS 27. Woot is covering the devices with a one year warranty in case there are any issues down the road. Read our review.
- Until the end of the day, you can grab an Ultraloq Bolt door lock for $74.99 from Amazon (usually $109.99). This Wi-Fi smart lock features both numerical and fingerprint sensors, giving you a few options for quickly unlocking your door. You can check the status and lock or unlock the door from your phone, and it integrates with other smart home platforms like Alexa, Apple Home, and Google Home.

This model is compatible with computers as well as Xbox consoles, although only games predating the Xbox Series S/X era will be able to be played directly from the drive. Newer games will need to first be copied over to your console’s speedy SSD.
- Woot is selling a variety of refurbished Apple Watch Series 9 units for as low as $189.99, depending on the configuration you choose. While they’re a couple of generations old, it’s rare to see recent models that low, and this is one of the older Apple Watches that will support watchOS 27. Woot is covering the devices with a one year warranty in case there are any issues down the road. Read our review.
- Until the end of the day, you can grab an Ultraloq Bolt door lock for $74.99 from Amazon (usually $109.99). This Wi-Fi smart lock features both numerical and fingerprint sensors, giving you a few options for quickly unlocking your door. You can check the status and lock or unlock the door from your phone, and it integrates with other smart home platforms like Alexa, Apple Home, and Google Home.
